summary:
FloodLens is a satellite-powered flood-awareness and surface-change monitoring platform developed for Lahore, Pakistan, using NASA-ISRO NISAR Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data. It processes satellite imagery through a Python-based geospatial pipeline to identify and visualize 337 candidate surface-change zones, classified by their proximity to the Ravi River corridor or likely agricultural areas.

The platform combines satellite observations with an evidence-grounded Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system that retrieves information from curated sources, including PDMA Punjab, NDMA Pakistan, Dawn News, and FEWS NET. Through an interactive React dashboard, users can explore candidate zones, inspect radar statistics, access advisories, and ask questions using an AI assistant that prioritizes source-backed answers.

FloodLens addresses the challenge of making complex Earth observation data accessible and useful for public awareness. Its defining feature is responsible communication: it distinguishes radar-detected changes from confirmed flooding or physical damage and clearly identifies when ground-verified impact information is unavailable.

By combining open satellite data, geospatial intelligence, and accessible public information, FloodLens aims to support informed disaster awareness and preparedness.
details:
FloodLens is a public flood-awareness and satellite intelligence platform developed for Lahore, Pakistan, using NASA-ISRO NISAR Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) observations.
The platform processes satellite GeoTIFF imagery through a Python-based geospatial pipeline to identify and visualize candidate surface-change zones. Its current T084 analysis identifies 337 candidate polygons, classified into two categories: 21 near the Ravi River corridor and 316 associated with likely agricultural areas. These classifications provide geographical context, not confirmation of flooding or damage.
FloodLens combines this satellite analysis with an evidence-grounded Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system that retrieves information from curated reports and sources, including PDMA Punjab, NDMA Pakistan, Dawn News, and FEWS NET. Its React-based interactive dashboard allows users to explore satellite observations, filter zones, inspect radar statistics, access advisories, and ask questions through an AI assistant.
